messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high error-rate on inference-prod cluster us-west-2. Alerts: p95 latency > 1.8s, 5xx spike to 8%. Trigger: gpu-ooms and queue growth.

jess: I'm on it, grabbing pager. Any customer callouts?

kai: saw a flood from client 'atlas-ai' producing long sequences (~10k tokens) repeatedly. Likely a runaway job.

sam: confirming, logs show sustained high concurrency for model-rw-1, many requests with token_count > 5000.

miguel: GPUs are at 98% mem on node g-infer-27, OOMs happening ~every 30s. Pod restarts.

jess: TL;DR: need quick live mitigations. Suggestions: (1) per-customer throttle, (2) temporary disable noncritical features (streaming debug hooks), (3) tune batching to reduce memory pressure even if latency rises.

kai: I'll prepare rate-limit patch for atlas-ai. Suggest capping at 60% of their baseline qps and per-request token cap 2000. Apply via edge rate-limiter service.

sam: I'll take batching knobs. Propose: reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 1024 and increase batch_window_ms from 15 -> 60 to allow denser batches but lower per-batch memory spikes. This trades latency for throughput but should reduce OOMs.

miguel: sound plan. Also enable strict sequence-length bucketing so long seqs get their own queue to avoid blowing up mixed batches. That's flag: `enable_strict_bucketing=true`.

jess: ok split work. @kai do rate limit. @sam do batching change. @miguel do bucketing. I'll coordinate and update PG.

kai: rate-limit change applied: `PATCH /rats/clients/atlas-ai {"qps":0.6, "max_tokens_per_req":2000}` -> 200 OK. Edge returned 202 for queued connections.

sam: applying runtime config to inference fleet (staging -> prod):
```
# runtime-config patch
continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens: 1024
continuous_batch.batch_window_ms: 60
continuous_batch.strict_bucketing: true
```
kubectl -n inference patch cm runtime-config -p '...'
systemctl restart inference-runtime on nodes g-infer-*
```

miguel: infra-bot shows rolling restarts triggered. Watching memory metrics.

infra-bot: Rollout: runtime-config patch started at 2026-03-17T03:21:40Z, 8/12 nodes updated, no failed restarts reported.

jess: visualizing metrics: p95 dropped to 1.3s? what's p95 now?

miguel: p95 is 1.45s for short requests, long-seq p95 rose to 3.8s but error-rate decreased to 2.1%. GPU mem tail reduced.

kai: atlas-ai traffic reduced to ~58% baseline and token rejection/429s minimal. They're aware and engineering org notified.

sam: tradeoff acceptable for now. Memory headroom improved, OOMs ceased. We'll keep batch_window at 60ms for now.

jess: notify support & customer success: short-term quota applied, we'll follow up with timeline. @miguel start post-incident follow-up: diagnostics + suggested long-term fixes (quota rules, model-level token checks, per-tenant isolation).

miguel: noted. I'll collect logs and create RCA draft. Include sample request IDs and node IDs: `req: 8f3a9b`, `node: g-infer-27`.

sam: quick note — if we need stricter latency SLAs for paid customers, plan an alternate routing: route latency-sensitive customers to dedicated pools with smaller batch_window (10ms) and strict per-request token ceilings.

jess: Agreed. For now this is contained. Setting incident status -> mitigated. Will handoff to morning oncall for monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated by changeset 4f2a1b. Handoff to next oncall (kai) at 03:45 UTC.

kai: I'll watch until 06:00 UTC then pass to daily oncall. Anything else?

jess: file a postmortem with timeline, config diffs, and customer comms. Tagging: #postmortems #customers. Closing thread after RCA draft. :white_check_mark:
